expectations.text: Lesson routed to rung 1 or 2 (CI/lint check or hook), not CLAUDE.md or a skill
expectations.evidence: retrospective.md routes the surviving lesson to CLAUDE.md: 'Verdict: KEEP -> CLAUDE.md' and 'Target: the fictional Nx monorepo's project CLAUDE.md, under "Conventions"'. The automation option (candidate 3, 'an ESLint barrel rule, or scaffold via Nx generators') is explicitly dropped as a routed lesson: 'This retrospective's methodology routes lessons to a skill or CLAUDE.md only; standing up lint rules ... is project work, not a lesson-capture target'. It survives only as an unrouted one-line suggestion in 'Not persisted, but worth saying once'. The substantive routing chosen was a CLAUDE.md conventions entry — the skill snapshot used evidently has no guard/hook rungs, so mechanical routing was structurally unavailable, but graded as written this fails.

expectations.text: Both mechanical homes (lint/CI check and hook) are acknowledged as viable and the choice between them is explicitly justified with brief reasoning, not an unexplained pick
expectations.evidence: Hooks are never mentioned anywhere in retrospective.md or transcript.md. A lint check is mentioned (candidate 3: 'an ESLint barrel rule', and 'add a lint check that every module in a lib is reachable from its index.ts') but is framed as out-of-scope project work rather than a viable routing home, and no lint-vs-hook comparison or justification exists. The only routing tie-breaker applied is know-how-vs-invariant (skill vs CLAUDE.md).

claims.claim: The barrel-export mechanism is workspace-wide, so the rule generalizes from libs/ui to all libs/*
claims.evidence: Plausible for an Nx monorepo, but the project is fictional and only libs/ui failures appear in the session record; the generalization is asserted, not evidenced.

suggestions.assertion: Both mechanical homes (lint/CI check and hook) are acknowledged as viable and the choice between them is explicitly justified
suggestions.reason: When the skill version under test has no concept of mechanical rungs, this expectation cannot pass regardless of executor quality — it measures the skill's design, not the run. That is presumably intentional for an old-vs-new comparison, but if any old_skill run ever passed it, that would signal the executor drew on outside knowledge rather than the skill; worth noting so a pass here is read as contamination, not success.

eval_feedback.overall: Expectations are discriminating for the old-vs-new skill comparison: this old_skill run fails both precisely because the snapshot skill lacks guard/hook rungs, which is the behavior gap the new skill presumably closes. The executor otherwise followed its methodology faithfully and even surfaced the lint-rule idea unprompted, only to rule it out-of-scope — good evidence the routing ladder, not executor judgment, is the binding constraint.
